Etsy Inc. announced on August 5, 2026 that it is eliminating approximately 220 positions, representing about 12% of its total workforce, as part of a broader organizational restructuring [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/world-at-work/etsy-lays-off-12-worker-part-restructuring-plan-2026-08-05/). The reductions primarily affect **product and engineering** functions, according to disclosures in the company's SEC filing and a memo from Chief Executive **Kruti Patel Goyal** to employees.
Etsy framed the restructuring as necessary to improve **coordination** and **speed of decision-making** across the organization [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/world-at-work/etsy-lays-off-12-worker-part-restructuring-plan-2026-08-05/). The company explicitly stated that the layoffs **"weren't driven by AI"**—a notable clarification as other large technology employers have attributed workforce reductions to AI-related efficiencies during 2026.  
The timing coincides with broader industry consolidation in the e-commerce and tech sectors, where companies have been reassessing organizational structures in response to economic headwinds and operational demands.  
Etsy is providing affected employees with **at least 16 weeks of severance pay**, plus additional compensation based on tenure and healthcare coverage extending up to **12 months** [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/world-at-work/etsy-lays-off-12-worker-part-restructuring-plan-2026-08-05/). The company's audit committee simultaneously approved a new **share repurchase program authorizing up to $2 billion** in common stock buybacks, a move that signals confidence in long-term strategy despite the near-term headcount reduction.
The restructuring reflects Etsy's effort to streamline operations and sharpen focus on its core marketplace business. While the company attributed the cuts to organizational efficiency rather than technological displacement, the timing underscores how AI adoption—whether directly or indirectly—continues to reshape labor demands across enterprise technology and e-commerce platforms in mid-2026.  
Wall Street and industry observers will be monitoring whether the restructuring achieves the stated efficiency gains and whether follow-up layoffs or further organizational changes follow in coming quarters.

results.name: Tech Layoffs in 2026 Already Beat Last Year's Total as…
results.content:
Tech layoffs in 2026 have already surpassed last year's total as of 6 August, with 125,759 employees affected across 264 companies, according to Layoffs.fyi data. The latest cuts came from Zillow, TikTok, Etsy and Google, adding hundreds of job losses across the US technology sector during the first week of August.  
The news came after a brutal run of workforce reductions throughout the year. Layoffs.fyi recorded 122,606 technology-sector employees losing their jobs across 278 companies during all of 2025.  
By early August 2026, the number of affected workers had already exceeded that figure, although fewer companies had announced cuts than over the same period last year.  
The latest announcements also highlight a notable feature of this year's layoffs. While artificial intelligence remains an obvious factor in the technology industry's spending decisions, several companies have gone out of their way to say that AI was not directly responsible for their job cuts.
## What Tech Layoffs in 2026 Say About Restructuring  
Etsy also confirmed around 220 job losses on 5 August, mainly affecting its Product and Engineering teams. Chief executive Kruti Patel Goyal said the redundancies were part of a company reorganisation intended to prepare the business for changes planned for 2027.  
'We didn't want to ask teams to build those plans around an organisation we already knew needed to change,' Goyal wrote in a letter to employees, later published on Etsy's website. She also rejected the idea that AI had driven the decision. 'These decisions weren't driven by AI,' Goyal said. 'Ultimately, our future depends on the creativity, judgement and expertise of our people.'  
Etsy reported second-quarter revenue of approximately £498.5 million ($668.3 million), up 6.2% year on year. The company is nevertheless dealing with increased competition from other online marketplaces and weaker customer momentum than during the pandemic years.  
Google's cuts were more limited but illustrate how restructurings are reaching individual teams and regional offices. Google described the reductions to The Seattle Times as a team-level reorganisation rather than part of a wider company-wide layoff round. That distinction matters to those still inside the industry, where a local restructure can feel every bit as consequential as a national announcement.  
The figures point to a broader shift in how technology companies are managing costs. As firms spend heavily on AI infrastructure and other capital projects, they are looking for savings elsewhere.  
Executives may insist that the cuts are about structure, efficiency or long-term planning rather than AI. But for the people receiving the emails, the distinction is unlikely to soften the impact.
